subject: SOC2 Type II request — subservice egress logs & billing reconciliation clarification
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@fintegrate.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Audit Team <audit@fintegrate.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC2 Type II + subservice clarifications for upcoming audit

Hi Monica —

Hope you’re well. Fintegrate Health is kicking off our vendor SOC review for our 2026 audit and we need Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report covering calendar year 2024 (or the most recent period you can share). In addition to the report itself, our auditors have a few carve-out / subservice clarifications before they accept the provider report:

- We need confirmation of which cloud provider reports (AWS/GCP/Azure) you are relying on as subservice organizations for network/storage/keystore, and whether those reports are scoped as a carve-in or carve-out for Redwood services.
- Specifically, we need to understand where egress logs (edge-to-customer traffic logs) are retained and for how long — auditors want an example export or sample file format.
- We also need details on billing reconciliation data (how Redwood reconciles cloud billing vs customer-facing usage for chargeback) — is a reconciled ledger export available?

Can you provide the SOC 2 PDF, a subservice mapping spreadsheet, and a small sample of the egress log export? If you have a standard bridge letter template that covers SOC 2 coverage and the audit window alignment for cloud providers, that would be helpful too.

Target timeline: our audit kickoff is 2026-11-29 — would appreciate materials by 2026-11-22 if possible.

Thanks — let me know if we should loop in procurement or security contacts.

Best,
Elena Morris
Director, Vendor Risk
Fintegrate Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Audit Team <audit@fintegrate.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II + subservice clarifications for upcoming audit

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the note and the timeline — we can support this audit. Quick answers up front, then I’ll attach the files your auditors asked for:

- SOC 2 Type II: attaching Redwood Inference SOC 2 Type II report for the 2024 calendar period.
- Cloud provider reliance: Redwood relies on AWS for primary compute and object storage, and GCP for long-term analytics; both are used in scoped systems. We also use a hosted KMS offering from CloudScaleOps (subprocessor). We’ll include the provider report references and note where the responsibility split is a carve-in (our controls) vs carve-out (provider controls).
- Egress logs: egress (edge) logs are captured at the load balancer and at the inference gateway; retention is 90 days by default, with 365-day archived snapshots for high-tier customers. I’m attaching a small sample export (redacted).
- Billing reconciliation: we maintain a reconciled usage ledger for all customers; exports are available in CSV. Reconciled line-items map tokens/embeddings to internal usage keys.

Attachments included: redwood_soc2_typeii_2024.pdf, subservice_mapping_2026.xlsx, egress_log_sample_1.json.

A couple of caveats for your auditors:
- Our SOC 2 report covers Redwood’s control environment for services operated by Redwood; we rely on provider SOC reports for the infrastructure layer. The subservice_mapping spreadsheet marks which controls are inherited.
- For CloudScaleOps (KMS), we have a subprocessor attestation but their SOC 2 report is only available under NDA — we can facilitate an auditor access request if needed.

If the auditors want formal confirmation, we can issue a bridge letter that calls out the audit windows for AWS/GCP and the subprocessor access path. Would you like our standard bridge letter or a tailored statement referencing the exact control numbers?

I’m looping in Rishi (infra security) and Kimberly (procurement) to confirm the KMS access cadence and billing export format.

Best,
Monica Patel
Sr. Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_soc2_typeii_2024.pdf, subservice_mapping_2026.xlsx, egress_log_sample_1.json
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:48:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: SOC2 Type II + subservice clarifications for upcoming audit — action items

Team — forwarding Fintegrate’s ask; short action list:

1) Rishi — please confirm exact retention windows and locations for egress logs (LB + gateway). Auditors want: storage path, retention policy, sample export format, and whether archived 365-day snapshots are stored encrypted with customer KMS keys or Redwood-managed keys.

2) Kimberly — please confirm whether billing reconciliation CSVs can be produced for customer-facing consumption (redacted version is fine) and provide the export schema. Also confirm if CloudScaleOps’ subprocessor NDA process is live so auditors can request their SOC 2.

Target to get back to Elena by 2026-11-18 to give auditors time.

Thanks — Monica
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC2 Type II + subservice clarifications for upcoming audit — action items

Monica / Kim —

Quick answers (technical):

- Egress logs storage:
  * LB logs: pushed to AWS S3 bucket s3://redwood-logs/egress/lb/YYYY/MM/DD — lifecycle rule transitions to Glacier after 30 days, delete after 365 days for archived policy.
  * Inference gateway logs: stored in GCP bucket gs://redwood-gateway-logs/egress/YYYY/MM/DD and exported to BigQuery for 90-day hot retention; daily snapshots to GCS Coldline for 365 days.
  * Encryption: LB S3 buckets use AWS KMS keys (customer-tied keys when customer has BYOK; otherwise Redwood-managed CMKs). Gateway archived snapshots encrypted with CloudScaleOps KMS (we have envelope encryption where we wrap with CloudScaleOps).

- Sample export: attached egress_log_sample_1.json — format is JSON lines with fields: timestamp, src_ip, dst_ip, bytes, request_id, customer_id_hash (sha256), region, path. We redact IPs and customer identifiers for external samples.

- Billing reconciliation: we can export a reconciled CSV. Schema includes: customer_id_hash, internal_usage_key, tokens_generated, embeddings_generated, infra_cost_allocated_usd, bill_period_start, bill_period_end. We can provide a redacted CSV for auditors; generating one takes ~2 business days.

- CloudScaleOps SOC access: procurement confirmed they will share SOC 2 under our standard subprocessor NDA; auditors can request direct access — Kimberly, can you confirm the link/process?

I’ll also provide the exact S3/GCS bucket ARNs and retention lifecycle rules if the auditors need them verbatim.

Rishi
Head of Infra Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: egress_log_sample_1.json
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC2 Type II + subservice clarifications for upcoming audit — action items

Monica / Rishi —

Confirmed the procurement items:

- CloudScaleOps access: auditors from Fintegrate can request the CloudScaleOps SOC 2 report via our vendor portal (https://vendors.redwood.com/cloudscaleops-request). We will submit the NDA on their behalf if they provide auditor contact. Lead time: typically 3-5 business days.

- Billing export: we have a self-service reconciled ledger export that can be generated and redacted. I’ve attached a small mock CSV (redacted_billing_export_sample.csv) and schema doc. We can schedule an export run and deliver by 2026-11-20 if Fintegrate approves.

- Bridge letter: we maintain a standard bridge letter for cloud provider alignment that references the provider report dates and scope; it includes language about inherited controls and any carve-out assumptions. If Elena wants a tailored bridge letter referencing specific control IDs, we can produce that but it will require a secondary review (2 business days).

I’ll wait for Elena’s preference and can route the CloudScaleOps SOC access once we have auditor contact info.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Vendor Risk Lead, Procurement
Redwood Inference
